info.title: Ossie HTTP execution proposal
info.description: DRAFT, not an adopted standard or a deployed service. Browser-oriented HTTP/JSON control plane and one materialized result delivered as a single Arrow IPC stream or immutable self-contained pages. All schemas are defined in execution.schema.json. Authentication is deployment supplied; this document does not implement an identity system.

get.summary: Discover the caller-visible contract and query capabilities

200.description: Capabilities for this authorized caller; declarations do not prove semantic conformance.

get.summary: Resolve an immutable data source binding

200.description: The id is data_source_id. This id MUST NOT be rebound to another model revision.

post.description: Submit one execution job, not separate sync/async jobs. Omitting Prefer means wait=0: return immediately with 202 unless already terminal (200). wait=N holds POST at most N seconds, returning terminal 200 or pending 202 for the same execution_id; the server may return earlier. Bounded wait optimizes fast completion without unbounded synchronous connections or mandatory polling round trips. It is neither an execution deadline nor a download timeout and never cancels the query. No automatic retries, query repair, native SQL escape, or idempotency guarantee. Pagination partitions the completed result, not the query: no page-size/offset clause; limit remains a semantic cap.

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: One wait=N preference; integer N from 0 through 60 and no greater than advertised max_wait_seconds. Bounds POST waiting only; expiry returns the same job without cancellation. Invalid or unsupported waits are rejected.

200.description: Terminal Execution: succeeded, failed, or cancelled. HTTP success alone does not imply query success. Success includes the entire immutable result manifest: exactly one of url or pages, subject to the client's 1 MiB control-JSON limit.

202.description: Pending Execution: queued, running, or cancelling. Poll using execution_id.

200.description: An Execution in any state; terminal states and manifests are immutable.

post.summary: Request best-effort cancellation without a request body
post.description: Idempotent for an execution. Completion may win the race. Cancelling is pending, not proof of cancellation. Aborting a local HTTP request does not invoke this operation.

200.description: Terminal Execution: cancelled, succeeded, or failed.

202.description: Pending Execution: cancelling or another currently observed pending state.

Id.name: id
Id.description: Opaque identifier, encoded as a single path segment. A binding id is data_source_id; a query id is execution_id.

Problem.description: Non-2xx failure using RFC 9457 ProblemDetails. status matches the HTTP status; error.code is the Foundation code directly. Redirects are not allowed.

x-result-download.url: Execution.result.url OR Execution.result.pages[i].url, only when state is succeeded
x-result-download.description: Dynamic absolute same-origin or explicitly allowlisted HTTPS URL, not a fixed API path or cursor API. Every download is one immutable self-contained IPC stream with required Ossie schema/field metadata; no concatenation, redirects, or Range requests. Server-selected page_index and row_offset are contiguous from zero; page row/decoded-byte sums equal root totals, including repeated schemas. No empty page except the sole page of a zero-row result; page bytes are positive. Every page has identical fields and actual physical types (including decimal scale and timestamp unit/timezone) and metadata except ExecutionMetadata page_index/row_offset, which must appear together and match its descriptor; both are forbidden unpaged. Cross-origin fetch omits account authorization and cookies. The same authorization, origin, and whole-result expires_at protections apply to each page. HTTP content compression is allowed; Arrow IPC buffer compression is not. Decode bytes before comparing counts. Selected-page browsing does not establish complete-result consumption; completeness describes the whole result. Explicit repeated reads before expiry are allowed, but no automatic retries, resubmission, link renewal, live execution rows, or Flight are defined.

x-browser-cors.description: Servers and result hosts must explicitly allow approved application origins and satisfy preflight requests. A token broker or backend-for-frontend is deployment infrastructure, not supplied by this package.
